Definition: properly, to thrum, i.e. beat a tune with the fingers; expectation. to play on a stringed instrument; hence (generally), to make music
BiblicalUsage: Nagan means to play a stringed instrument, to thrum a tune with the fingers, and it is used where music meets the Spirit. In 1 Samuel 16:16 the servants look for a cunning player on the harp to play when the evil spirit is upon Saul, and in 2 Kings 3:15 Elisha says, bring me a minstrel, and when the minstrel played, the hand of the Lord came upon him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe music can open a door for the word of the Lord, because Elisha asked for a player before he asked for a prophecy; the harp does not replace the word, but it can quiet the room for it.
